basis: Unsigned x64 native Rust/Tauri GUI; no archive overlay or embedded executable payload was found. PE resources contain version data, icons and a manifest.
Recovered all five Brotli-compressed Tauri assets. The 1925112-byte JavaScript bundle contains the JJSploit interface, React/Redux, Monaco editor code, and game Lua script buttons.

The interface offers Roblox attachment, Lua script execution, ESP, aimbot, movement modification, script-file editing, an autoexec folder shortcut, and an explicit Reset action that closes the game and queues removal of the application Documents folder.

Native bootstrap reads the dependency list from https://wearedevs.net/tauri.json, maintains Documents/jjsploit dependencies and db.json, and loads WRD.dll with LoadLibraryExW. Native wrappers resolve Attach, Execute, RunExternal, ExternalAttached, ExternalCommand and SetSettings through GetProcAddress.

The UI and native DLL-load failure path explicitly ask the user to disable antivirus and Smart App Control. These are suspicious requests; the reviewed prompts do not themselves change those settings.

Frontend telemetry posts {app,category,label,version} to the vendor appevent endpoint and includes Google Analytics page/action events. No credential-store collection or unrelated exfiltration path was identified in the reviewed application code.

The downloaded WRD.dll and other remote dependencies are absent from the supplied executable and were not fetched or executed. Their behavior cannot be established from this file. A game exploit frontend that downloads native dependencies and asks users to disable protections is inappropriate for benign training; the supplied bytes do not prove a separate hostile payload.
